body:
CANONICAL: installing an Engram build and cutting stores over (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, consolidating 4 earlier notes). The controlling text is AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, Authority and Git, and docs/features/full-store-migration.md. Greg, 2026-09-22: "ideally we don't want to have interruptions".

1. JUDGE THE CHANGESET FIRST, because `readiness` checks only schema and policy admission, not what rows contain.
- Durable rows change (a mapped column, a record reshaped under its id, data named as retired, a durable derived row such as runtime heads, status or work projection blobs computed differently, a retired schema object, or a projection the new build no longer declares): import must teach the conversion by name with counts, and EVERY live store needs migration export and import (one-way, ids unchanged, the old file kept as the backup), WHATEVER readiness reports. `different_build_schema` is one signal of this case, not its definition.
- Only the derivation of a table or search index that projection repair rebuilds changes (CORE_REBUILDABLE_SCHEMA_OBJECTS: object_fts, project_memory_state, project_memory_advertisements, core indexes; REBUILDABLE_WORK_SCHEMA_OBJECTS: work_catalog_fts and the rebuilt work projection tables; src/storage/open_schema.rs repair_rebuildable_projections): treat every live store as `projection_repair_required`. Stop that store's consumers, run `engram doctor --repair-projections` with the new build, restart the consumers on it. After a DDL change, older builds can no longer open the repaired store. spec.md, shipped.md and sqlite-store.md still say repair touches only indexes, triggers and FTS, which is stale.
- Migration steps: export with the old build and import with the new; tell the active sessions first, choose a window when they are idle, stop every consumer, convert, and swap the files, keeping the old store file as the backup.
- Repair and migration interrupt sessions: say so when presenting the changeset, and stop to ask Greg (rules-authority-and-landing).
2. READINESS ON EVERY LIVE STORE with the new build, from each repository's folder. Count ~/.engram/projects before each landing rather than trusting a list: one store was missed once, and another appeared without notice. Live stores as of 2026-10-01: Engram (098f58cc…, C:\github\Personal\Engram), PhoenixCodeNav (98bc0e74…, restored 2026-09-26; Phoenix tracker records from 2026-09-23 05:17 to 2026-09-26 12:41 local are lost), TermAl (8764cc68…, created 2026-09-27 for the Beads migration; its scratch homes under TermAl's .tmp\bx are not live), CV (12ea2770…, appeared about 2026-10-01 03:24Z).
3. THE ORDINARY CASE (ready, no durable change): build the release from the committed tree, rename the installed C:\Users\grzeg\.cargo\bin\engram.exe aside into C:\Users\grzeg\.engram\backups\ under a name carrying a UTC stamp with Z and the old build (recent landings use engram-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<old build12>.exe, so backups sort by time), and copy the new one in. Use the explicit .exe path: in Git Bash `cp` to the suffix-less name writes a file called `engram` that Windows cannot start (happened 2026-09-27). Verify from PowerShell (`engram --version`, `(Get-Command engram).Source`) as well as Git Bash, and confirm the version shows the landed revision with no +dirty. Skip the swap if the build is byte-identical. Stop nothing: running MCP servers and control sidecars keep the old build until they exit (see the restart routes in rules-restart-and-review). Stopping every engram.exe would interrupt live agents (control_unavailable, paused queues).
4. A migration tool run must never see engram.exe change mid-apply (two builds writing one store).
